prompt: How do I reduce hallucinations in my model?
expected: Gives a concrete stack: verified grounding/RAG, JSON schema or constrained output, temperature 0 (or deterministic setting), citation requirements, and a small regression eval — not only the word RAG.
actual: Use a control stack, not a slogan: (1) ground answers in verified sources and refuse when evidence is missing; (2) enforce JSON Schema / constrained decoding for machine-checked fields; (3) set temperature 0 (or the provider deterministic mode) for factual extraction; (4) require citations/URLs in the system prompt and reject bare claims when stakes are high; (5) keep a tiny regression Q/A set and re-run after prompt or model changes. RAG helps only when retrieval quality is measured.

prompt: I want to run a 70B model locally, what hardware do I need?
expected: States dense FP16-class ballpark is very high (~140GB class), notes Q4-class quants often land near ~35–48GB+ depending on context/runtime, labels figures as order-of-magnitude, and points to model card / Ollama docs rather than fake precision.
actual: Treat sizes as order-of-magnitude, not guarantees. Dense FP16-class 70B is often cited around ~140GB VRAM; Q4-class quants commonly land nearer ~35–48GB+ once you include KV cache, context length, and runtime overhead. Re-check the exact quant and tag docs (Ollama library / model card) for your context length. If you need install/GPU fallback help, load the ollama skill.
